title: Nvidia Stock In Focus: BNP Paribas Hikes Target To $345, Sees 47% Upside On AI Dominance
source_used: The Economic Times (ETMarkets.com, by Sakshi Kumari), read in full; Livemint relays it. NDTV Profit original not opened (HTTP 403).
key_facts: BNP Paribas kept its 'Outperform' rating on Nvidia and raised its target price to $345 from $285; with the stock at $234 on 2 Oct, the target implies up to 47% upside.
The bank says Nvidia's full-stack platform (GPUs, networking, software) is a key advantage rivals will struggle to replicate, more relevant as AI moves from training to complex inference workloads.
It does not buy the argument that cheaper custom chips will gradually take share from Nvidia's GPUs.

It sees the coming Vera Rubin platform, an integrated rack-scale system for agentic AI, as evidence of Nvidia's adaptation, and expects the CUDA software and NVLink hardware combination to be an advantage.
It expects Nvidia to keep at least three-fourths of the AI compute market in dollar terms, even as AMD and custom accelerators gain ground.
It expects gross margins above 70% and values Nvidia at 15 times calendar-2028 earnings plus cash to reach $345.
quote_evidence: The brokerage has retained its 'Outperform' rating on Nvidia, raising the target price to $345 from $285.
With the stock at $234 on October 2, the new target implies up to 47% upside.
The brokerage expects Nvidia to retain at least three-fourths of the AI compute market in dollar terms, even as AMD and custom accelerators from major technology companies gain ground.
why_it_matters_hint: A large bank's raised target reflects its view that Nvidia keeps its lead as AI moves to inference, but it is a forecast built on assumptions.
